note: Braids' SAW_COMB has exactly two axes. TIMBRE is parameter_[0] and it is the COMB PITCH: digital_oscillator.cc:248 reads `pitch_ + ((parameter_[0] - 16384) >> 1)`, i.e. -64..+64 semitones about the played note, so it maps to the engine's TIMBRE. COLOR is parameter_[1] and it is the FEEDBACK: digital_oscillator.cc:261-263 forms `(parameter_[1] << 1) - 32768` and warps it through ws_moderate_overdrive, so it is bipolar and it maps to the engine's HARMONICS. MACRO sits at 0.5 in every case -- ApplyMacro(0.0, 0.6, -0.6, macro) returns tilt 0 at noon, which is Braids' flat loop. MORPH sits at 0.0, NOT at noon: saw_comb_engine.cc:127-128 sets waveshape = 0.5 + 0.5*morph and pw = 0.5 - 0.25*morph, and VariableShapeOscillator is a plain saw at waveshape 0.5 with pw 0.5, so MORPH 0 is the AnalogOscillator OSC_SHAPE_SAW exciter of macro_oscillator.cc:366-369 and MORPH 0.5 is a half-square at 37.5% duty, which the module cannot make. SPEC R11 allows this (MORPH has no detent), but it does mean noon is not stock on this engine. The morph-noon-not-stock case at the end exists only to pin that number; it is deliberately off-axis and is not a fidelity claim.
auditNote: AUDITED 2026-07-29 by an independent pass. Findings folded back in: (a) two cases were ADDED -- comb-clamp-highest and comb-clamp-highest-res -- because no case in the original file reached a played note high enough for the module's comb-pitch ceiling (ComputeDelay, digital_oscillator.cc:74-76, MIDI 128) to engage, and the port has no such ceiling. That corner is off by nearly an octave of comb pitch and by ~30% of the reference's energy, and it was the largest unmeasured deviation in the engine. (b) res-ringing's justification was FACTUALLY WRONG about the module's maximum feedback and has been rewritten: ws_moderate_overdrive tops out at 32728, not 32766, so the module's loop is sub-unity and the port's is exactly unity. (c) The engine header's DECLARED DEVIATIONS block is accurate on its own three points and is NOT restated here, but note that saw_comb_engine.h is hashed into package_digest (plaits_lab_catalog/validate_catalog.py:31-37), so the header edit that added that block has already moved this engine's published digest; nothing further was written to it by this pass, and these corrections live here and in README.md instead.
tolerances: Tolerances are set to what the SHIPPED engine achieves, not to the ~1 dB / ~1.5 dB / ~1 cent target. Every case looser than the target is loose for one of two measured, reported reasons, both of which are undeclared deviations in the DSP rather than tolerance slop. (1) COMB PITCH QUANTISATION. Braids smooths the comb pitch with the integer recursion `filtered_pitch = (15 * filtered_pitch + pitch) >> 4` (digital_oscillator.cc:250-252) in 1/128-semitone units. Because `>> 4` floors, every f in [p-15, p] is a fixed point, so rising from the Init() state of 0 the filter STALLS 15 LSB = 11.72 cents FLAT of the requested comb pitch and stays there. The engine's float one-pole (saw_comb_engine.cc:89) converges exactly, so its comb sits 11.72 cents sharp of the module's and its delay is 0.680% short. Measured directly: at note 45 / TIMBRE noon the module's effective comb delay is 879.05 samples @96 kHz where ComputeDelay returns 873.12; the port's is 873.1-equivalent. Consequence: the module has a comb null on the 70th harmonic (7.7 kHz at note 45) that the port does not have at all. (2) OUTPUT CLIPPER. Braids ends with `CLIP(out)` (digital_oscillator.cc:278), a hard clip at full scale; the engine ends with SoftClip (saw_comb_engine.cc:151-152), which is SoftLimit below +-3 and therefore attenuates everywhere -- SoftLimit(1.0) = 0.778. Rebuilding the engine in a scratch tree with only these two lines reverted moves the stock case from AC RMS -1.25 dB / spectrum 1.10 dB / 5-10 kHz +10.18 dB to AC RMS -0.00 dB / spectrum 0.39 dB / 5-10 kHz -0.27 dB, with every band from 80 Hz to 10 kHz inside 0.5 dB. Neither line is changed here.

cases.name: TIMBRE noon, HARMONICS noon
cases.why: The comb sits on the played note and the feedback is ~0, so this is the pure FIR comb the README describes: 0.5*dry plus one echo, audible, not silent. It is also the case the comb-pitch quantiser hurts most, because the module's 11.72-cent stall puts its comb null on the 70th harmonic while the port's exact delay puts no null anywhere. That is the +10.18 dB in 5-10 kHz (3.6% of energy). The -1.25 dB AC RMS is the SoftClip: the reference peaks at 1.000 and the port at 0.775 = SoftLimit(1.0).

cases.name: TIMBRE 0 at note 45 -- delay clamped
cases.why: Bottom of the TIMBRE axis. comb_note = 45 - 64 = -19, so both sides run into their delay clamp -- Braids at 8192 taps @96 kHz (digital_oscillator.cc:256-258), the port at kSawCombDelaySize-2 = 4094 @48 kHz. This is the case that proves the README's 'clamps below MIDI ~70 just as it does on hardware' claim, and it is the tightest case in the file precisely because a clamped delay is identical on both sides and the quantiser stall cannot move it.

cases.name: TIMBRE 0 at note 84 -- delay NOT clamped
cases.why: The same TIMBRE end, above the MIDI ~70 knee, so the delay is live rather than clamped: comb_note = 20 = 25.96 Hz = 1849 taps. 4.0 dB spectrum is far outside the target and is the comb-pitch quantiser at its worst: 11.72 cents on a 1849-tap delay is a 12.6-tap offset, so the two combs' null ladders are half a null out of step by ~1.3 kHz and stay interleaved for the rest of the band. The energy-weighted mean is 3.57 dB with individual bands at +4.49 and -6.25 dB, and the sign alternates band to band, which is the signature of interleaved nulls rather than a level or bandwidth error.

cases.name: TIMBRE 1 at note 45
cases.why: Top of the TIMBRE axis: comb_note = 45 + 64 = 109, a 17-tap delay. Together with comb-lowest this pins the direction and the full +-64 semitone span; a sign error or a halved range would put this case tens of dB out rather than 1 dB. AC RMS is the SoftClip again, at the same -1.27 dB as the stock case. NOTE: at note 45 the top of TIMBRE is comb_note 109, which is BELOW the module's comb-pitch ceiling, so this case cannot see the clamp deviation -- see comb-clamp-highest.

cases.name: TIMBRE 1 at note 84 -- past the module's comb-pitch ceiling
cases.why: ADDED 2026-07-29 BY THE AUDIT PASS, because nothing in this file reached this corner. `comb-highest` runs TIMBRE 1 at note 45, where comb_note = 109 and both sides are free-running; here comb_note = 84 + 64 = 148 and the two sides diverge by nearly an OCTAVE. Braids' ComputeDelay opens with `if (midi_pitch >= kHighestNote - kOctave) midi_pitch = kHighestNote - kOctave` (digital_oscillator.cc:74-76), and for the DigitalOscillator kHighestNote is 140*128 and kOctave is 12*128, so the comb pitch CEILINGS at 16384 = MIDI 128 = 7.2236 taps @96 kHz = 13.29 kHz. saw_comb_engine.cc has no equivalent: its only ceiling is CONSTRAIN(delay, 2.0f, ...) at line 95, which does not bind until MIDI ~150, so at TIMBRE 1 on note 84 the port's comb sits at 21.15 kHz. Measured: 10.24-20.48 kHz reads -8.18 dB while carrying 19.1% of the reference's energy, and 5.12-10.24 kHz reads +3.85 dB. This is a REPORTED, UNFIXED DSP deviation, not tolerance slop -- 2.4 dB is where the shipped engine sits, and it is reachable by any played note above MIDI 64 with TIMBRE toward its top.

cases.name: DIAGNOSTIC: the same ceiling with the comb resonant
cases.why: ADDED 2026-07-29 BY THE AUDIT PASS. The same missing ceiling as comb-clamp-highest, with HARMONICS at 0.9 so the comb has a resonant PEAK rather than shallow nulls, which is what makes the size of the deviation unmissable: 4.27 dB spectrum, with 10.24-20.48 kHz at -13.19 dB carrying 21.7% of the reference's energy and 5.12-10.24 kHz at -7.67 dB carrying 8.1%. Roughly 30% of the module's energy sits in a resonance the port does not have, because the module's comb is pinned at 13.29 kHz and the port's is at 21.15 kHz. 4.5 dB is FAR outside the ~1.5 dB target and is NOT a fidelity claim -- it is a pinned number holding a reported defect at a fixed value so a fix can be measured. No cents tolerance: a 13-21 kHz ring against a 1046 Hz saw is inharmonic and the autocorrelation estimator is not usable, exactly as in high-note.

cases.name: HARMONICS 0 -- full negative feedback
cases.why: Bottom of the COLOR axis. This is the case that proves the feedback is genuinely BIPOLAR and not a 0..1 resonance: `(parameter_[1] << 1) - 32768` is -32768 here, so the loop inverts. 4.2 dB spectrum: with |g| near 1 the comb is a resonator, not an FIR comb, so the 11.72-cent comb-pitch error moves sharp resonant peaks rather than shallow nulls -- the 5-10 kHz band carries 26.2% of the reference's energy and reads -10.06 dB because the module has a resonance there that the port puts elsewhere. The -2.53 dB AC RMS is the worst level error in the file and is SoftClip acting on a resonantly-boosted signal.

cases.name: HARMONICS 1 -- full positive feedback
cases.why: Top of the COLOR axis. CORRECTED 2026-07-29: an earlier revision of this file said Braids' warped knob reaches g = 32766/32768 and that BOTH loops sit at unity. It does not, and they do not. `resonance` is 32766 only BEFORE the warp; Interpolate88 then reads ws_moderate_overdrive at index 65534, and that table's last two entries are 32728, 32728 (braids/resources.cc) -- so the module's maximum feedback is 32728/32768 = 0.99878 and its loop DECAYS. The port's WarpResonance(1.0) = 1.016129 * SoftLimit(2.0) = 1.0000 exactly, so the port's loop is marginally stable and does not. That is a real, unreported deviation of the same class as the comb-pitch floor: a truncated table entry reproduced as its closed form. It is the reason the two HF bands above 2.5 kHz (5.0% of energy combined) read +14 dB -- the port's ring builds to an equilibrium set only by its in-loop clip while the module's is bounded by a real sub-unity pole -- and it is why 2.8 dB is not a tolerance a fix would tighten by hand-waving. The fundamental band, 36.8% of the energy, matches to -0.07 dB.

cases.name: HARMONICS 0.85 with the comb detuned up
cases.why: Strongly resonant but short of the unity corner, and off the TIMBRE detent, so it exercises both axes together in the region a player actually uses. Passes near the target.

cases.name: HARMONICS 0.15 with the comb detuned down
cases.why: The negative-but-not-extreme quadrant, on the other side of noon from res-high and at a different note, so a swap of the two Braids parameters cannot survive this case together with res-high. Loose for the same comb-pitch reason: at comb_note = 60 - 32 = 28 the delay is 594 taps and 11.72 cents is a 4-tap offset.

cases.name: TIMBRE swept 0 to 1
cases.why: The whole comb-pitch axis in one render, which averages the per-null disagreement away and so measures the axis MAPPING rather than its fine structure: 0.73 dB. An inverted or rescaled TIMBRE would not average out.

cases.name: HARMONICS swept 0 to 1
cases.why: The whole feedback axis, inverted through FIR comb to ringing, in one render. The two sub-80 Hz bands read -22 to -24 dB and carry 1.4% of the energy between them: that is the subsonic wander a comb with positive feedback and no DC blocker parks in its line, which the header discusses -- both sides have it, at different amplitudes, because the in-loop clip is the only thing bounding it and the two clippers differ. It is below the 20 Hz band edge in musical terms and is not what this case is measuring.

cases.name: Both axes mid, two octaves up
cases.why: No cents tolerance, deliberately. comb_note = 84 + 19.2 = 103.2 is a 15-tap delay ringing at ~3.2 kHz against a 1046 Hz saw, so the strongest periodicity in the signal is inharmonic with the note; ab_compare's autocorrelation locks the reference to 1046.0 Hz and the port to 262.3 Hz, a pure octave-quadrupling artefact of the estimator rather than a pitch error. Every other case in the file reads inside 0.7 cents, which is where the R5 rate check actually lives.

cases.name: DIAGNOSTIC: the port's per-note reset has no counterpart in the module
cases.why: ADDED 2026-07-29 BY THE AUDIT PASS. Every other case in this file runs triggerHz 0, so nothing here exercised saw_comb_engine.cc:79-81 -- and Braids' SAW_COMB is the right control, because MacroOscillator::Strike() reaches DigitalOscillator::Strike(), which only sets strike_, and RenderComb never reads it. The module is therefore COMPLETELY INERT under a trigger, and any difference here is the port's alone. READ THE BANDS, NOT THE HEADLINE: the energy-weighted figure is 0.48 dB only because the affected bands carry 0.0% of the reference's energy. `--bands` shows 20-40 Hz +22.40 dB, 40-80 Hz +25.70 dB, 320-640 Hz +23.72 dB against a module that has essentially nothing there. That is the port's per-note reset -- the R15 delay-line clear, the exciter_.Init() phase reset, and in particular `comb_pitch_ = 48.0f` (line 59), which at note 84 forces a 36-semitone comb glide at the start of every note through a 4 ms pole. The line clear is deliberate and defended in Reset()'s own comment; the FIXED 48.0 seed is not, and is the avoidable part. The 1.0 dB spectrum tolerance holds the headline where it is; it is deliberately NOT a claim that this case is clean.

cases.name: DIAGNOSTIC: MORPH at noon is not the module
cases.why: DELIBERATELY OFF-AXIS -- this is not a fidelity claim, it is a pinned number. Identical to the stock case except MORPH is at noon, which gives waveshape 0.75 and pw 0.375: a half-square exciter at 37.5% duty, not the module's saw. Spectrum goes 1.10 -> 1.86 dB and the 320-1280 Hz bands go from -0.8 to -2.9 dB, so a user who leaves MORPH at its centre position is a measurable distance from Braids. Kept so that the claim is re-runnable with one command.
